sources.cite: Advanced Trauma Life Support, 10th edition (American College of Surgeons, 2018): classes of hemorrhage and adult blood volume about 7% of body weight
sources.note: Relayed from the CMSRN case postop-hemorrhage-early-signs, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the CCRN Adult bleeding case (CCRNADULT/bleeding-after-whipple, read 2026-11-10); not re-read. Class I under 15%, II 15-30%, III 31-40%, IV over 40% of blood volume; heart rate rises and urine output falls before the systolic pressure does (class II). FLAG: the model's vital-sign anchors follow the classic table and are a teaching simplification.

sources.cite: Carson JL, et al. Red Blood Cell Transfusion: 2023 AABB International Guidelines. JAMA 2023;330(19):1892-1902
sources.note: Relayed from the CMSRN case postop-hemorrhage-early-signs, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-14 (PubMed abstract) for the course seed. The restrictive thresholds (7 g/dL; 8 with preexisting cardiovascular disease or orthopedic surgery) are for hemodynamically stable hospitalized adults, not active hemorrhage.

sources.cite: Rossaint R, Afshari A, Bouillon B, et al. The European guideline on management of major bleeding and coagulopathy following trauma: sixth edition. Crit Care 2023;27:80
sources.note: Relayed from the CMSRN case postop-hemorrhage-early-signs, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-16 in the publisher's PDF (Crit Care 2023;27:80, doi:10.1186/s13054-023-04327-7, open access, from Universidad Europea's repository; summarizing fetch with quotes). Recommendation 9 (Grade 1B): 'We recommend the use of repeated Hb and/or Hct measurements as a laboratory marker for bleeding, as an initial value in the normal range may mask early-phase bleeding.' Used for one teaching point: a single normal hemoglobin does not rule out early bleeding.
